chunks: Muhammad ibn Bukran al-Naqqash (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani, client of Bani Hashim, narrated to us. He said: Ubayd ibn Hamdun al-Ru'asi narrated to me. He said: Husayn ibn Nasr narrated to us, from his father, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from al-Husayn ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them all).
He said: I complained to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) about a debt that I had, and he replied:
O Ali! Say: "O God! Enrich me with Your lawful provisions away from Your forbidden things, and through Your grace make me independent of all others."
For even if your debt were the size of Sabir, God would settle it on your behalf. Sabir is a mountain in Yemen, and there is no mountain in Yemen more majestic or magnificent than it.

key_terms.أَغْنِنِي بِحَلَالِكَ عَنْ حَرَامِكَ: Enrich me through Your lawful provisions away from Your forbidden things — the core du'a for debt relief and spiritual protection from haram
key_terms.صَبِيرٌ: Sabir — the largest and most majestic mountain in Yemen, used here as a measure of the enormity of debt God would settle
key_terms.مَوْلَى: Mawla — client/freedman, denoting Ahmad al-Hamadani's social status as a freed slave affiliated with Bani Hashim

ai.seo_question: What supplication did the Prophet Muhammad teach Imam Ali for relieving debt?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) narrates that he once complained to the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) about a debt weighing on him. The Prophet taught him a powerful du'a: asking God to make one self-sufficient through lawful means and independent of all except God. The Prophet assured Ali that this supplication, if recited, would bring divine aid in clearing even the most mountainous of debts — using the famous mountain Sabir in Yemen as a hyperbolic measure.
word_analysis: al-Baqir (the one who opens up knowledge)
